apps.subtitle: Windows games on iPhone and iPad
apps.localizedDescription: A fast, controller-friendly launcher that runs Windows games on iOS and iPadOS with Steam and GOG built in, powered by Wine, FEX and Metal via DXMT.

versions.localizedDescription:
**BCD is in alpha:** an early stage of development, before beta. Many games run, many do not yet, and things can break between builds. When a game fails, please send a log.

## Red Dead Redemption 2

- **No processor time lost on exceptions.** RDR2 asks Windows for the time tens of thousands of times a second, and every one of those calls used to take an exception that BCD caught and answered: about 20,000 a second through the tick count, and up to about 18,000 more through timer calls in the game's own process, which Rockstar's launcher starts. Both now run as plain calls, so a performance core no longer goes to exceptions and iOS has less reason to lower the processor clock.
- **Rockstar's launcher off the fast cores sooner.** The launcher, its Social Club helper and its service move to the efficiency cores one second after the game starts drawing instead of after a minute, leaving the performance cores and the power budget to the game.
- **New recommended settings.** BCD's own diagnostics sample less and its helper threads run on the efficiency cores; the game gets a larger memory pool, the swap file for game data only and faster Direct3D 12 paths. These settings held 30 FPS on a 12 GB iPhone. On the game's page use **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended** to get them.

The two time fixes help GTA V and every other 64-bit game too (below); the sooner launcher move and the new settings are RDR2's own.

## Also in this build

Vulkan for 32-bit programs, GOG games of the older download kind, a newer Steam client for the games that need it, and a long list of fixes from testers' logs. Everything new is off until you turn it on, except the fixes.

## Faster

- **64-bit games no longer pay for asking the time.** Windows programs read the tick count from a shared page at a fixed address that iOS does not allow, so every `GetTickCount` and `GetTickCount64` call cost an exception that BCD caught and answered. Red Dead Redemption 2 asks about 20,000 times a second, enough to keep a performance core busy and make iOS lower the CPU clock sooner. BCD's 64-bit kernel32 now reads the same page directly: the same values, no exception. On for every 64-bit program; `env.MADEIRA_USD_DIRECT = 0` restores the old path.
- **Games started by a launcher stop taking exceptions on library calls:** a program that another program starts (RDR2 and GTA V Enhanced from Rockstar's launcher, Social Club's helper) now calls between Windows' own libraries directly, as the first program always did. Before, each such call took an exception, for example every timer call through `timeGetTime`: up to about 18,000 a second in RDR2. Together with the tick count fix above, RDR2 no longer spends a performance core on exceptions. `env.MADEIRA_AUX_IAT_HEAL_CHILD = 0` turns it off.
- **Direct3D 12 sampler cache:** identical samplers are created once. On by default; `sampler-cache = 0` turns it off.
- **Time zones:** a program that asks for the local time no longer makes Windows look up the time zone each time.
- **Thread registers:** a program that reads its threads' registers often (a garbage collector, a profiler) no longer makes BCD read its settings files each time.

## New

- **Vulkan for 32-bit programs:** the same `vulkan = moltenvk` line that gives a 64-bit game Vulkan now works for 32-bit games too.
- **GOG: older downloads.** A GOG game that only has GOG's older kind of download (Return to Castle Wolfenstein, the Quake games) now installs, updates and repairs in BCD's GOG downloader, with the same pause, resume and progress as the others.
- **BCD Dock: newer Steam client (September 2026).** Some games ask for a newer Steam interface than the January 2026 client has (Grim Dawn, Hades II, Enshrouded). **Settings › BCD Dock › Newer Steam client** installs the September 2026 client. BCD renames the old client folder (nothing is deleted) and moves your games, saves and settings into the new one. Off by default.
- **Steam Friends through BCD Dock:** your friends list, their status, invites and joining a friend, through Valve's own client. Off by default.
- **GOG Galaxy features for a GOG game:** a GOG game's sign-in, achievements, statistics, leaderboards and play time, per game. Off by default (`env.BCD_GOG_GALAXY = 1`).
- **KosmicKrisp:** a second Vulkan driver for a game's `vulkan` line, on iOS 26. Off by default.
- **Shader compiler for wgpu games:** a 64-bit game built with wgpu on Direct3D 12 can compile its shaders with the DirectX Shader Compiler that BCD builds, where Wine's compiler cannot (skate.'s PC port). Per game (`env.MADEIRA_OPTIN_DLLS = dxcompiler`); auto-tune adds it after that failure.
- **Run-time compiled Direct3D effects**, **Direct3D 9 luminance render targets** (opt-in) and a **Japanese locale per game**.
- **New opt-in switches for Direct3D 9, 10 and 11** (the libraries built from source: 32-bit games and the 64-bit `D3D11_SRC` set): dropping shader objects after use (`dxmt = d3d11.keepShaderIR=0`), a later Direct3D 9 readback (`env.DXMT_D9_LATE_READBACK = 1`), shared textures inside one process (`env.MADEIRA_D3D11_LOCAL_SHARE = 1`), typeless texture compression (`env.DXMT_TYPELESS_COMPRESSION = 1`) and two command-list memory switches (`env.DXMT_CMDLIST_KEEP_BLOCK`, `env.DXMT_DYN_KEEP`).
- **Direct3D 12:** concurrent compute encoders, off unless `cs-concurrent = 1`.
- **CPU features:** `env.MADEIRA_FEX_CPUID_CLASSIC = 2` reports 1 GB pages as well as the two older bits of `1`.
- **Two experimental 64-bit sets built from BCD's own source,** both off by default:
  - `env.MADEIRA_WIN64_FRESH = 1`: Wine's 64-bit libraries rebuilt with every BCD fix. Before, some of those fixes reached only 32-bit games: a message box that ignored its timeout, the reasons a signature check failed, and which file a failed import came from.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DXMT_FRESH = 1`: the 64-bit Direct3D 10/11 libraries rebuilt the same way, including the fix for a GPU hang with geometry and tessellation shaders.
- **Very large reservations (The Witcher 3 DirectX 12, HITMAN (2016)):** `oversize-reserve-virtual = 1` gives a game that reserves 64 GB or more a range nothing else of the game can land in. This was the cause of The Witcher 3's DirectX 12 crash 13 seconds in. The recommended settings of both games turn it on.

## Fixes and improvements

> **Tried a game on an earlier build? Reset its settings first.** On the game's page: **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**, then check that **Options › Auto-tune › Auto-tune this game** is on.

- **JIT:**
  - with the method on **Automatic**, BCD now uses its own helper once this device is paired with BCD, even when StikDebug is installed. In testers' logs, 8 of 109 StikDebug memory requests were never answered, against none of 248 for BCD's helper. If the device refuses BCD's pairing, the same attempt goes on with StikDebug;
  - two **Enable JIT** requests at once now share one helper instead of starting two;
  - **Check setup** that meets a developer disk image another step has just installed tries once more.
- **After iOS closes a game for memory:** pressing Play right after BCD reopens now waits up to 5 seconds for the verdict on the session that was closed, so its new settings apply to this start.
- **Lock handling:** BCD no longer releases a lock that a running thread still holds. Every game now uses the safer mode that GTA V, RDR2 and the Horizon games already used; this fixes freezes and crashes after such a release.
- **Direct3D 11:** the 64-bit Direct3D 11 library used by the launchers of RDR2 and GTA V Enhanced, and by games with `D3D11_SRC`, gets three fixes the 32-bit one already had:
  - short constant buffers;
  - 16-bit index ranges;
  - a tiny fullscreen window.
- **Direct3D 9, 10 and 11** (built from source): compute views are restored with the rest of the state, anisotropy is kept in range, Direct3D 10's start instance and the index buffer query are right, a resolved view reports its mip count as Windows does, and a Direct3D 12 device that presents through Vulkan gets its swap chain (`env.MADEIRA_DXGI_VK_SWAPCHAIN = 0` turns this off).
- **LEGO City Undercover:** the fix for a layer format Metal refuses now reaches 64-bit Direct3D 11 through the `D3D11_SRC` set (its recommended settings use it).
- **Direct3D 12:** a pipeline that Metal refuses because of its dual-source blend is built again without those factors (Freddy's House, Poppy Playtime, ReSkate).
- **64-bit programs that do not fit:** a 64-bit program file that finds no room under BCD's own reserved area gets one more try without that limit (GTA IV's Rockstar Launcher; `env.MADEIRA_IMAGE_RELAX = 0` turns it off).
- **Windows:**
  - network and random-number calls into memory iOS does not let the kernel write now work;
  - a pipe's state can be set on a unix pipe;
  - a setup program no longer asks for its install media again and again;
  - the free space of a drive iOS reports as 0 falls back to the file system's own figure;
  - a request for token information outside the table is refused instead of read past it;
  - in 32-bit programs: a lock's waker no longer touches a waiting thread's freed queue entry, and an exception handler removed while the one before it ran is no longer called.
- **Windows Vulkan:** a game started from the library or through BCD Dock now finds Vulkan.
- **Freezes:** the Windows server no longer reads settings or writes a log line while a game thread is paused (Requiem: Avenging Angel, Counter-Strike Nexon).
- **Emulator:**
  - a program that ends no longer runs on into freed memory (Football Manager 27);
  - an optional exact mode for 64-bit x87 integers.
- **Sending logs:**
  - the comment box of **Send Log** no longer hangs;
  - a log carries more of a game's own error reports (a Java fatal error report, Unity's console, a message repeated without end shown once) and, after a session that did not end cleanly, how it ended.
- **GOG:**
  - an update or a repair no longer writes a support file over a game file that was right;
  - a GOG installer in a game folder is no longer listed as a game.
- **Find games:** a game's crash handler or crash reporter no longer becomes its card (Timberborn from an external drive).
- **Launchers and installers** that cannot be started as a game point to the Desktop's Start menu.
- **Game page notes:**
  - a game in a folder whose name Windows' older file functions cannot read;
  - a game that needs glide2x.dll.
- **Messages:**
  - a game closed by iOS for memory says by how much;
  - a JIT shortcut that cannot be found is no longer an error.
- **Steam:** malformed data from Steam is refused instead of stopping the app.
- **FFmpeg** updated to 7.1.5.
- **Auto-tune** knows many more cases from testers' logs. Among them:
  - protected programs that rewrite their own code (Undisputed, Football Manager 27, Hitman: Blood Money, the Street Fighter 6 demo, Euro Truck Simulator, Persona 3 Reload);
  - The Witcher 3's DirectX 12 crash;
  - the Steam interface a game misses;
  - StikDebug requests that were never answered.

## Games: fixes from testers' logs

Most of these settings were made from testers' logs and have not been tried on a device yet. A game you set up on an earlier build gets them with **Reset to Recommended** (see above). Please send a log either way: it is how the next step is found.

**Past the wall they stopped at:**
- **Persona 3 Reload:** the logos and movies flashed (a flat colour or diagonal streaks); the recommended settings fix how the video picture is read and bring the settings the game was tested with.
- **Kingdom Come: Deliverance II:** the game ended with "Failed to load the Game DLL": its game library needs Windows' Restart Manager, which BCD's 64-bit set did not give every game. The recommended settings add it.
- **Dying Light: The Beast:** the renderer saved its pipelines through a pipeline library it never got, and crashed. BCD now answers that call for the game and reports Direct3D feature level 12_1, which the renderer asks for first.
- **MECCHA CHAMELEON:** the engine's loading thread asked for the audio devices before starting Windows' COM and called through the empty answer. Such a thread now gets a shared COM apartment.
- **HITMAN (2016):** the game asks for a 64 GB block of address space and shrank the request a little after every refusal: 3 million refusals in six minutes and no picture. The new very large reservation serves it.
- **The Witcher 3 (DirectX 12):** it crashed 13 seconds in, because its 64 GB area overlapped another of its own blocks. The new reservation keeps that area free.
- **Fernbus Simulator:** its first atomic write into its own program faulted on BCD's copy of the program; the program now runs from where it was loaded.
- **Anodyne:** its .NET runtime writes code into its own pages, and every one of those writes was emulated (4 million in 30 seconds, no picture). Those pages are now plain memory for this 32-bit game.
- **State of Decay: Year-One Survival Edition:** the engine stopped at "Unsupported video card detected!"; the game now sees a GeForce GTX 1060, a card it knows.
- **Wreckfest** and **DEMON'S TILT:** they read the first entry of an empty display list and crashed. The virtual monitor now has a name and a list of modes (Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy went from none to 20 with the same settings).
- **Day of the Tentacle Remastered:** it draws with OpenGL only; its settings turn on BCD's OpenGL.
- **DOOM 3: BFG Edition:** it threw an error when BCD shortened OpenGL's list of extensions (a fix for older id Software games); it now gets the whole list.
- **LEGO City Undercover:** iOS closed BCD at the first frame, because the game asked for a picture format Metal does not show. The 64-bit Direct3D 11 library with the fix is now the game's.
- **Rise of the Tomb Raider:** the game makes a picture buffer more than two billion pixels tall, and every frame failed. Its Direct3D 11 library now refuses that buffer as Windows does.
- **skate. (PC port):** its shaders did not compile with Wine's compiler; the game now uses BCD's DirectX Shader Compiler.
- **Mewgenics:** its sound came short; BCD's audio timing is changed for this game.

**Protected games** (the protection reads Windows' shared system page):
- **Final Fantasy Resonance** and its demo, **Planet Coaster 2**, **Planet Zoo 2**, **ONIMUSHA: Way of the Sword** and **Resident Evil Requiem:** the protection now reads its registers as the game left them. Planet Zoo 2 and ONIMUSHA also get a fixed place for their large program. Planet Zoo 2 then stops after it contacts its server; no setting is known for that yet.
- **Football Manager 27** and **Hitman: Blood Money:** the emulator translates one block of code at a time inside them (Football Manager 27's plugin made a wrong pointer inside its copy protection; Blood Money's packer ran twice).

**Memory on smaller devices:**
- **Dark Souls III** (devices under 10 GB): expanded compressed textures took the game to iOS's memory limit. The largest level of every compressed texture is now dropped on those devices only (slightly softer textures). On a 6 GB phone, lower the game's texture quality as well.
- **Firewatch** (under 10 GB): A15 iPhones expand compressed textures four to eight times; the largest level is dropped near the limit.
- **OPERATOR** (8 GB): iOS closed it at the limit while it loaded; its two largest texture levels are dropped.
- **Half Sword demo** (under 12 GB): large memory blocks go to the swap file.
- **Metal Gear Solid 2 (Master Collection)** (6 GB phones): after the title it played a video without the decoders it needed and ran out of memory; its settings turn on BCD's video playback for it.

**Logs that say more** (settings that collect what the next fix needs): **Bugsnax** (it stops after its first frames: leave it 90 seconds on the first screen, then send the log), **Quaver** ("already running"), **Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker** (black picture), the **Resident Evil Requiem** demo, **Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy** (now past its empty display list, next a crash at its second swap chain), **Unreal Tournament: Game of the Year Edition**, **Clair Obscur: Expedition 33** (which also tries a video library Unreal may need) and **Project Zomboid** (a Java fatal error; it also tries a stricter memory order in the emulator, which is slower).

## Known issues

- **Foldable iPhone:** installed directly, iOS shows BCD in a small window on the inner display, because BCD is still built with the iOS 26 SDK. Inside LiveContainer it fills the screen.
- **Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare** reserves more address space than any iPhone or iPad gives and stops early. No setting changes this yet.
- **Heavy games after a few minutes:** iOS lowers the processor clock after a few minutes of heavy play, even when the phone is not hot. A game that needs much of the processor loses frame rate then: in The Last of Us Part I it about halves after three to four minutes.

Install help, game reports and ideas: the BCD-Games Discord is open, https://discord.gg/43TmupTVug
